title: The Morning Brief: Cameroon's breakthrough, Scheffler's dominance, and turmoil at LIV
dek: The morning brings celebration in African soccer, momentum in professional golf, and mounting financial pressure in the LIV Golf league as vendors report deep unpaid invoices and the Saudi funding tap closes this month.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Cameroon won its first Women's Africa Cup of Nations title by defeating Malawi 3-0, Scottie Scheffler opened the PGA Tour playoffs with an eight-shot victory, and LIV Golf faces acute liquidity stress as unpaid vendor invoices pile up and its Saudi backing ends.
bottom_line: Cameroon's first Wafcon title rewrites African women's soccer's championship ledger, Scheffler's eight-shot playoff victory establishes early momentum in the FedEx Cup race, and LIV Golf enters a critical phase as vendor payment disputes mount alongside the Saudi funding closure this month. The honest read: LIV's silence toward contractors and legal responses to demand letters, combined with WARN Act filing and restructuring executives on the board, suggests the league is navigating acute financial pressure beyond normal operations. Watch whether BC Partners' investment closes before vendor claims escalate into court filings; any delay risks formalized restructuring. The coming days will also surface final timelines for Swanson and Tyson, confirm Michigan State's official announcement of Bartholomae, and show whether Infantino's legal eligibility survives FIFA governance committee review.
body: Three continents, three divergent stories: one historic breakthrough, one dominant performance, and one financial crisis accelerating. The common thread is consequence, immediate for some, arriving soon for others.

Cameroon claimed its first Wafcon title Sunday in Rabat with a 3-0 victory over Malawi, ending a 22-year championship drought marked by three previous final losses to Nigeria. Marie Ngah Manga scored twice and Naomi Eto added one goal in the decisive match at Moulay Hassan Stadium. Manga's double moved her level with Temwa Chawinga and Barbra Banda on five tournament goals. The victory breaks a pattern and signals strength heading toward the 2027 World Cup.

Separately, Scottie Scheffler opened the PGA Tour's postseason with an eight-shot victory at the FedEx St. Jude Championship at TPC Southwind, closing on a 4-under 66 to finish 17-under 263. The margin stands as the largest in the tournament's 68-year history at that venue. Si Woo Kim finished second at 9-under. The win secured Scheffler the No. 1 seed through next week's BMW Championship and an additional $23 million in bonus money beyond the $3.6 million event purse.

The morning's third major story carries sharper edges. LIV Golf contractors and vendors report unpaid invoices ranging from thousands to nearly $100,000, with minimal response from the league's accounts receivable and legal departments, according to reporting from Front Office Sports. One contractor stated: "There's no response from the accounts receivable department. Even their legal counsel has not responded to demand letters." The withholding coincides with the Saudi Public Investment Fund's April announcement that it will cease funding LIV after this season. The league has filed a WARN Act notice signaling potential mass layoffs and is exploring funding from BC Partners' credit division. One Canadian streaming technology vendor claims LIV owes it more than $1.1 million for breach of contract and unpaid invoices. Full-time employees have not reported missed paychecks, but LIV has issued 30-day termination notices to some contractors. CEO Scott O'Neil said this month that the PIF "has been a tremendous steward of this business," yet the convergence of unpaid vendor invoices, termination notices, restructuring specialists on the board, and the WARN Act filing suggests liquidity pressure that goes beyond standard cash-flow timing.

Elsewhere: New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson suffered a right hamstring injury during Thursday's joint practice with Jacksonville and could miss approximately two months, according to NFL Network sources, a timeline that would sideline the No. 8 draft pick through at least Week 6. Chicago Cubs shortstop Dansby Swanson has a Grade 2 oblique strain and is expected to miss four to six weeks, per ESPN sources, potentially eliminating him from the remainder of the regular season. Michigan State is finalizing a deal to hire Dan Bartholomae, Western Michigan's athletic director since 2022, to fill the vacancy created by J Batt's departure to Kentucky. O.J. Brigance, the Baltimore Ravens' longtime player engagement adviser and Super Bowl champion linebacker, died August 17 at age 56 after a 19-year battle with ALS, having survived far beyond his initial 2-5 year prognosis. The Scottish Football Association announced it will not vote for FIFA president Gianni Infantino in 2027, joining England, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland and aligning with UEFA's 55 member associations, which have threatened a World Cup boycott. The Premier League will publish full verdicts from its Key Match Incidents Panel on referee and VAR decisions this season for the first time. The AFL Tribunal upheld Jacob van Rooyen's three-match suspension for a striking incident that knocked out Port Adelaide's Aliir Aliir, rejecting Melbourne's appeal and the club's biomechanist evidence.
